summary: The never-callout compile behavior was added by the change. The fixed old harness cannot select it afterward; the same obligation did not exist before.

claims.necessity_reason: After the change, PCRE2 supports rejecting explicit callouts through a compile-context option, but the old target has no route to set it.

before.requirement: Rejection of explicit (?C) callouts through PCRE2_EXTRA_NEVER_CALLOUT with error 203 was not a supported behavior before this change.
before.reason: The before-version extra-option mask lacks the bit, and its complete callout parser proceeds directly to parsing the callout without the new rejection guard.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The before-version compile-error enum ends at ERR102, consistent with the absence of this specific rejection result.

after.requirement: Compilation can select PCRE2_EXTRA_NEVER_CALLOUT and reject explicit (?C) callout syntax with error 203.
after.reason: The after-version parser checks the new compile-context bit and returns ERR103. The fixed target only sets a compiled-length limit on that context, so generated input cannot enable this behavior.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The parser reads extra options from the compile context passed by the target.
ERR103 is the error assigned by the new parser guard.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: The second compile pass changes ordinary compile options and reuses the same context.

claims.comparison_reason: The same option-controlled rejection tuple is absent before and required but unreachable afterward. Ordinary callout compilation before the change is a different behavior.
